notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — three correctness issues (one confirmed panic on attacker JSON, two probes for spec-shape assumptions in RFC 5280 lints) plus seven maintainer-burden traps in API shape and OSCAL emission. None block 1.0; all benefit from being closed before downstream consumers pin pkix-lint into their build.
Confidence: 25% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: PKIX-7f92.2 (serial-length 1-octet-off — depends on x509-cert SerialNumber semantics I could not verify without reading x509-cert source) and PKIX-7f92.3 (AlgorithmIdentifier PartialEq — depends on x509-cert behavior, no in-tree negative fixture). Uncertainty driven by: x509-cert's internal normalization behavior on decode (SerialNumber sign-byte stripping, AlgorithmIdentifier parameter Some(Null) vs None handling) — I read pkix-lint's claims about these but did not cross-verify against x509-cert. The OSCAL parse/emit round-trip is well-tested. The deviation/runner/lint mechanics are well-tested. Would raise confidence if: (1) x509-cert SerialNumber::as_bytes documented length contract; (2) a hand-crafted negative-path AlgorithmIdentifier fixture confirmed §4.1.1.2 lint shape; (3) a fuzzing target on the cert_sha256_hex deserializer that runs in CI.
API contract risk: HIGH — six issues at P1 that are pre-1.0-free to fix but post-1.0 would each force a major version bump: serde_json::Value leak across 6 OSCAL APIs (.29), wrong round-trip contract (.38), Send+Sync assertions cover only 1 of 13+ types (.26), Severity Ord derive already broke in 0.8 (.24), OSCAL parser ignores claimed version (.33), x509-cert Name leak in DeviationScope constructors (.30). Two further P1s are smaller but type-system-leak shaped (ParseError derives .25). All 18 contract findings represent genuine caller footguns rather than stylistic preferences; none are pure opinion.
API contract confidence: 22% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: (1) PKIX-7f92.38 — the round-trip-lossy claim depends on oscal/mod.rs's stated contract; if the function-level rustdoc on deviation_store_from_risks has a priority-carve-out I missed, this would downgrade from 'documented contract violated' to 'documented behavior'; (2) PKIX-7f92.41 — whether check_shape per-call allocation is actually a hot path depends on caller usage patterns I cannot see; if all callers cache LintProfile outputs caller-side, the concern shrinks; (3) PKIX-7f92.27 — whether LintProfile and LintClone trait sealing is intended or accidental depends on the maintainer's plan for downstream profile crates (pkix-lint-cabf, pkix-profiles). Uncertainty driven by: (a) lack of access to consumer code that depends on these APIs — no real caller exists yet, so the 'production caller' lens is hypothetical; (b) the OSCAL feature gating choices (.34) may have rationale I am missing; (c) AGENTS.md's non-negotiable #6 (cache-friendly result types) frames most of my immutability/leakage findings — if the maintainer prefers a different interpretation of #6, several P1s would downgrade. Would raise confidence if: (1) a consumer crate existed and exercised these APIs; (2) cargo-semver-checks were run pre-1.0 to surface lurking surface-area issues; (3) doc-tests existed for the OSCAL round-trip claim so .38 could be empirically confirmed.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — pkix-lint reads as idiomatic Rust with localized rough edges. The main idiom holdouts are: (1) two HashMap-iterated-as-Vec patterns in lib.rs filter_to_ids and the redundant double-pass in check_unique_ids — signals 'gave up on a borrow checker fight that wasn't actually there'; (2) hex_encode in deviation.rs allocates per byte where the sister hex() in oscal/emit.rs does it right — duplicate-code hazard previously called out in .14; (3) a Vec<&Finding> return where impl Iterator is the natural shape — leaky abstraction smell; (4) clippy::uninlined_format_args holdouts in oscal/emit.rs and rfc5280.rs — mechanical fix. None of the findings reach REWRITE territory. The Lint trait shape, LintClone supertrait, DeviationStore add/find pipeline, and OSCAL parse error enum are all idiomatic. The crate is well above the median for a 1.0-trajectory Rust library.
Rust idiom confidence: 30% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: (a) PKIX-7f92.51 Clone derive on LintRunner — depends on whether the LintClone blanket impl's Send+Sync+'static bounds permit derive(Clone) to compile under all current downstream Lint impls; I confirmed the bounds match but did not actually try cargo check; (b) PKIX-7f92.50 missing From impls — the 'right' shape depends on whether the maintainer wants pkix-lint::oscal::parse::ParseError to be a 'leaf' error type (no From, by design) or a 'gather' type (From-rich); I assumed gather based on the existing wrap-by-source variants but could be wrong; (c) PKIX-7f92.45 filter_to_ids — I read the existing code as defensive scaffolding for a lifetime fight that doesn't exist, but it's possible the author had a specific Box<dyn Lint>-move scenario in mind that forced this shape. Uncertainty driven by: (1) did not run cargo clippy --fix on the suggested replacements to confirm they actually compile; (2) did not exhaustively scan rfc6125.rs, rfc8398.rs, rfc8551.rs, oscal/profile.rs, oscal/catalog.rs (~6000 LOC) — sampled their format! and panic shapes only; sub-findings may exist there in the same uninlined-format-args / Vec-where-iterator categories I already covered for lib.rs and emit.rs; (3) the existing 41-finding pass and this 10-finding rusty pass converge on similar themes (cache-friendliness, derive completeness), so the marginal new signal is approaching the bikeshedding floor — at 52 total findings on a 13K-LOC crate, further iteration is unlikely to surface novel issues. Would raise confidence if: cargo clippy --all-targets -W clippy::pedantic were run with the output cross-referenced against this finding set.
Crypto-security supplement (2026-05-14): 3 findings filed (PKIX-7f92.52 P2, .53 P3, .54 P3).

Sections covered:
- Section A (key material lifecycle): N/A — pkix-lint handles no secrets
- Section B (side-channel hygiene): N/A — no secret comparisons in scope
- Section C (untrusted input at protocol boundaries): 2 new findings — .52 (unbounded cert content interpolated into Finding detail strings), .54 (unbounded OSCAL parse strings). Existing .1 (cert_sha256_hex UTF-8 panic) and .6 (unix_to_rfc3339 panic) already cover the panic-on-untrusted-input class.
- Section D (random source quality): N/A — pkix-lint uses no RNG
- Section E (persistent storage of secrets): N/A — pkix-lint persists no secrets
- Section F (logging output safety): N/A — pkix-lint does not log directly; Finding output is intentional audit content; cert bytes are public; operator-supplied justification/authorized-by are operator responsibility not pkix-lint defect
- Section G (algorithm and parameter choice): 1 finding — .53 (UUID v8 seed concatenation without length prefix in finding_seed/risk_seed). SHA-256 choice, namespace separator discipline, and namespace literal hygiene all OK. EvidenceKey::seed correctly uses tag-byte discriminators; finding_seed and risk_seed do not — that is the asymmetry .53 captures.

Crypto-security confidence calibration: ~10% chance a third-party crypto reviewer finds a P0 I missed. Lower than typical (25%) because pkix-lint's threat model is narrow — no secrets, no key material, only attacker-influenced input parsing. Sections read in full (not diff-only): C, F, G. Sections E was N/A by inspection of dependencies. Possible misses: (1) idna crate timing in rfc8398 mailbox equivalence — moot because cert content is public; (2) BER/DER re-encode canonicalization in cert_sha256_of — documented behavior, audit-only impact.

Time spent: ~25 minutes. Bikeshedding floor: at 54 total findings on this 13K-LOC crate, marginal new signal is at the floor. Stopping per AGENTS.md guidance.
Crypto-security dedup pass: of the 3 supplement findings, 2 (PKIX-7f92.53 UUID seed, PKIX-7f92.54 OSCAL parse unbounded strings) were structural duplicates of PKIX-hy2e.41 and PKIX-hy2e.40 from the prior crypto-security pass on the previous pkix-lint review epic. Independent re-discovery confirms the issues persist 8 days after first filing. Duplicates closed with cross-references. Net new from this supplement: 1 finding — PKIX-7f92.52 P2 (unbounded cert content interpolated into LintResult::error detail strings) — not covered by the hy2e pass. This is the meaningful new signal.
